record.paper_title: What Regulates Galaxy Evolution? Open Questions in our Understanding of Galaxy Formation and Evolution.
record.context_brief: Model extensions for upcoming galaxy-evolution data
record.original_question: How should next-generation galaxy-formation models be extended to exploit upcoming resolved spectroscopy, atomic hydrogen, and molecular-gas observations, including explicit treatment of the transition from atomic to molecular gas, possible modeling of spatially resolved physical properties, and detailed chemical evolution with abundance ratios as constraints?

evidence.quote: In order to make the best use possible of the overwhelming amount of data that will come in the next future, our theoretical tools need to be updated including an explicit treatment of the transition from atomic to molecular gas, and (possibly) an explicit modelling of spatially resolved physical properties.
metals (including detailed abundance ratios) still represent a underutilized, yet very powerful constraint to models of galaxy formation and evolution
Therefore, the new generations of galaxy formation models and simulations should all include an explicit and detailed treatment of the chemical evolution of different species.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Develop a next-generation framework for modeling galaxy formation and evolution that can be quantitatively confronted with upcoming observations of resolved optical/near-infrared spectroscopy, atomic hydrogen (HI) 21-cm surveys, and molecular-gas (e.g., CO) surveys. The framework should specify and justify:

1. An explicit prescription for the transition between atomic (HI) and molecular (H2) hydrogen in the interstellar medium, expressed as a function of local physical conditions (gas surface density, metallicity, radiation field, pressure, etc.), and incorporated self-consistently into the star formation law used by the model.

2. A treatment of spatially resolved physical properties of galaxies (gas, stars, star formation rate, metallicity), going beyond global one-zone descriptions, suitable for comparison with integral-field spectroscopic surveys and resolved gas maps.

3. A detailed chemical evolution module tracking individual elemental species (not only total metallicity), including yields from Type II and Type Ia supernovae, AGB stars, and stellar winds, accounting for finite stellar lifetimes, so that abundance ratios (e.g., [α/Fe], [N/O], [C/O]) can be used as observational constraints on star formation histories and feedback.

The problem is to construct such an extended model (analytical, semi-analytical, or hydrodynamical) and to demonstrate that it simultaneously reproduces, within observational uncertainties, the statistical distributions and scaling relations of (i) HI and H2 content of galaxies, (ii) spatially resolved star formation and metallicity profiles, and (iii) stellar abundance ratios across galaxy mass and morphological type.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a broad open research program in galaxy formation theory. While individual components (HI/H2 transition prescriptions e.g. Krumholz-McKee-Tumlinson; resolved semi-analytic models; chemical evolution with detailed yields) have been developed and partially integrated in models such as L-Galaxies (Henriques+/Yates+), GAEA (De Lucia+), SHARK, and hydrodynamical simulations (IllustrisTNG, EAGLE, FIRE, SIMBA), no single model fully and consistently reproduces all observational constraints listed. The overarching goal therefore remains open as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: GAEA: chemical evolution and abundance ratios
status_evidence.snippet: Extensions of semi-analytic models including detailed chemical evolution and HI/H2 partitioning continue to be actively developed.
status_evidence.claim: Component-level progress exists but the integrated program remains ongoing.

status_evidence.title: Krumholz, McKee & Tumlinson HI-to-H2 transition
status_evidence.snippet: Analytic prescriptions for the atomic-to-molecular transition have been incorporated in many galaxy formation models.
status_evidence.claim: HI/H2 prescriptions are available and increasingly standard.

status_evidence.title: SIMBA / IllustrisTNG / EAGLE simulations
status_evidence.snippet: Cosmological simulations include resolved properties and metal tracking but tensions with observed abundance ratios and resolved scaling relations persist.
status_evidence.claim: Full simultaneous match to all listed constraints not achieved.
